title: Onboarding acceptance rubric: KV-cache, quantization, and prompt calibration
author: Ethan Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This page defines a prescriptive acceptance rubric for promoting new models (or model variants) into Redwood Inference service stages where the combination of KV-cache behavior, quantization profile, and prompt calibration can materially affect customer-facing quality and cost. It bundles automated checks, sample workloads, and explicit rollback triggers so model owners and SREs can make deterministic release decisions.

Context and goal
----------------
When a model is introduced or migrated (new weights, quantized artifact, or cache strategy) it may introduce subtle regressions: prefix-coherence loss, embedding drift, KV cache miss amplification, token-cost regressions, or tail-latency spikes. This rubric targets three cross-cutting failure modes we see most often in onboarding:
- Cache degradation: higher-than-expected cold-start miss rate or KV eviction-induced coherence regressions.
- Quantization artifacts: hallucination frequency increase, coherence loss for long context, or numeric instability in functioncall args.
- Prompt mismatch: previously calibrated prompt templates that relied on tokenization or temperature defaults behaving differently.

Acceptance philosophy
---------------------
- Gate first on safety & correctness (do not promote a model that increases hallucinations or safety alerts beyond SQC thresholds).
- Gate second on user-impacting regressions (coherence, functioncall correctness, embedded search recall).
- Only after quality gates are satisfied evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs and operational mitigations (adaptive KV-cache sizing, mixed-precision fallback).

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Model owner (author): prepares artifact, provides baseline metrics, and runs offline eval harness.
- Applied ML evaluator: runs the acceptance tests and annotator QA for flagged slices.
- Serving runtime owner: validates KV-cache plumbing and deployment knobs.
- SRE oncall: signs off on rollout plan, monitors live metrics during canary.

Pre-promote checklist (automated and manual steps)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Artifact metadata and reproducibility
   - Provide model artifact SHA, quantization recipe (bits, per-channel/per-tensor, lambda), and tokenizer snapshot.
   - Provide a reproducible Docker image or bundle for private/dedicated deployments.

2) Unit and regression tests (pass/fail)
   - Unit tests: tokenization parity, deterministic seed runs for N=3 seeds show low variance (response divergence < 0.02 normalized JS).
   - Regression probe suite: run full prompt-slice baseline (see Sample workload set below).

3) Safety & correctness gates
   - Safety sentinel pass rate >= baseline - 0.5 percentage points OR delta flagged and annotated with mitigation plan.
   - Functioncall integrity: 99.5% of functioncall responses must preserve schema and required keys on synthetic contract tests.

4) Coherence and semantic fidelity
   - Coherence index (see Metrics section) relative delta <= 1.5 points for high-sensitivity slices.
   - Named-entity recall for QA-style probes: delta <= 3% absolute.

5) KV-cache stability checks
   - Cold-start miss amplification: measured miss-rate in micro-sim shadow < 1.25x baseline for 95th percentile context length.
   - Eviction churn (evictions per minute per model instance) <= baseline + 10%.

6) Quantization-specific checks
   - Token-level perplexity increase <= 6% on calibration corpus.
   - Calibration-driven hallucination delta <= 0.8% absolute on adversarial probe set.
   - Per-layer numeric anomaly scan: no layers with activation overflow/underflow events in stress runs.

7) Prompt calibration and token budget checks
   - Tokenization drift (prompt -> token count) <= +5% for canonical prompts.
   - Temperature/Top-p sensitivity: response variance must be within expected band given same sampling settings.

Sample workload set (must be run under the eval harness)
------------------------------------------------------
- Canonical customer prompt family (N=10k probes): intents across translation, summarization, code-completion, and multi-turn chat.
- Long-context stress set (N=2k): 8k–32k token priming, measuring KV-cache hit/miss and tail-latency.
- Functioncall contract set (N=500): schema-anchored calls that assert type and key presence.
- Adversarial coherence set (N=1k): purposely perturbations and priming traps to surface hallucination regressions.

Metrics and explicit thresholds
-----------------------------
All metrics below are measured relative to the baseline model (the currently promoted artifact in stage). Absolute thresholds are listed where appropriate.
- Safety sentinel delta: +0.5 pp tolerated; >+0.5 pp requires annotated mitigation and manual review.
- Coherence index (0–100): high-sensitivity slice delta <= 1.5 points; medium slices <= 2.5.
- Embedding drift (cosine similarity mean on canonical corpus): delta >= -0.02 tolerated; worse requires embedding rebaseline plan.
- Cold-start miss-rate (micro-sim, 99th pct): <= 1.25x baseline.
- Eviction churn (evicts/min/instance at 95th pct): <= baseline + 10%.
- Token cost delta (per-token expected cost): <= +12% tolerated with cost-contingency plan.
- Tail-latency (p99 generation time): <= baseline * 1.2.
- Functioncall schema failure rate: <= 0.5% absolute.

Example acceptance table (pass/fail guidance)
----------------------------------------------
| Gate | Measure | Pass condition | Action if fail |
|------|---------|----------------|----------------|
| Safety | Safety sentinel | delta <= 0.5pp | Reject; escalate; security review |
| Coherence | Coherence index (high) | delta <= 1.5 | Hold; targeted annotation run |
| KV-cache | Cold-start miss 99p | <= 1.25x baseline | Reduce cache pressure; increase per-tenant TTL; re-eval |
| Quant | Token-level perplexity | <= 6% increase | Try per-channel quant; fallback to mixed-precision |
| Prompt | Tokenization drift | <= +5% | Re-calibrate prompts; update canonical templates |

Operational runbook for marginal passes
--------------------------------------
When a model passes quality but violates cost/latency knobs, use an adaptive rollout:
1) Canary: 1–2% traffic for 24 hours with tight telemetry (coherence, safety, cost, p99 latency).
2) If any SQC alert fires, hold traffic and run fast rollback (see Rollback triggers).
3) If cost delta > +8% but quality unchanged, enable:
   - Token budget hard-limits via Redwood Console route config.
   - Dynamic batching aggressive thresholds for low-latency slices.
   - Mixed-precision fallback for non-critical tenants.

Rollback triggers (automated)
----------------------------
- Safety sentinel rate increase > +1.0 pp over baseline within rolling 30m window.
- Coherence index drop > 3.0 points on any high-sensitivity slice within 60m.
- Tail-latency p99 increase > 40% sustained for 15m.
- Eviction churn > baseline + 25% for 10m.
If triggered: stall the rollout, immediately execute rollback job (repoint route to previous artifact), create incident ticket with priority = P0 and notify owners.

Telemetry and dashboards to verify during canary
------------------------------------------------
Create a dedicated canary dashboard with these panels:
- Safety sentinel rate (per-tenant) 1m/5m/30m windows.
- Coherence index time series by slice and tenant.
- Cold-start miss-rate histogram and 99th percentile.
- Eviction churn (evicts/min) heatmap by instance.
- Token cost trend (per-route tokenized count * cost per token).
- P99 generation latency and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Functioncall schema failures with detailederror samples.

Calibration procedure for prompts (step-by-step)
----------------------------------------------
1) Run canonical prompt family through tokenization snapshot for both baseline and candidate; compute tokenization drift.
2) For any prompt with drift > +5%, run a priming-level A/B test locally to measure semantic alignment.
3) For templates that are token-compact vs token-expanded, produce two calibrated variants and include routing hint in route config for tenant-level overrides.
4) Update canonical prompt registry with the chosen token-stable variants and mark as locked for the rollout.

Quantization remediation playbook
--------------------------------
If quantization causes a quality regression:
- Immediate actions: increase representative calibration dataset size (add adversarial probes), switch from per-tensor to per-channel where supported, and/or relax clipping.
- Medium-term: re-run mixed-precision hybrid compile with explicit layer exclusions for sensitive layers (embedding and attention-key layers).
- Long-term: maintain a quant-failure catalog mapping probe-to-layer-susceptibility to speed future remediation.

Post-promotion monitoring & 72-hour checklist
--------------------------------------------
- 0–1h: Verify telemetry ingestion and alerting correctness.
- 1–8h: Monitor safety and coherence slices every 30m and annotate anomalies.
- 8–24h: Compare embedding drift across representative tenants; run lightweight shadow probes.
- 24–72h: Review cost impact and eviction patterns; finalize any token-budget mitigations.

Annex: example CLI commands and curl checks
-------------------------------------------
- Run shadowed micro-sim to estimate cold-start miss-rate:
  ./eval-harness/bin/micro_sim --model candidate:sha=abc123 --workload longcontext --out report.json

- Run functioncall contract tests (examples):
  curl -X POST https://eval.local/api/run_contract -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_KEY' -d '{"model":"candidate:abc123","suite":"functioncall_contract_v1"}'

- Quick check for prompt tokenization drift (python snippet):
  from tokenizer import Tokenizer
  t = Tokenizer('tokenizer_snapshot_v42')
  baseline_tok = t.encode('canonical prompt')
  print(len(baseline_tok))

Contacts and escalation
----------------------
- Model owner: listed on artifact manifest (required).
- Applied ML evaluator oncall: applied-ml-eval@redwood.ai
- Serving runtime SRE: runtime-sre@redwood.ai
- Pager: Redwood SRE rotation (P0).

This rubric is authoritative for all model promotions that modify quantization, tokenizer snapshots, or KV-cache strategy for public and dedicated deployments. If you need exceptions, open a formal risk review with security and product and document mitigation steps in the related page.
